summary: Romantic interactive Valentine’s Day love-story slideshow website with soft pastel design, smooth transitions, floating hearts/sparkles, star+moon animations, and gentle background music—now specified as an 11-page flow with a “cute boy with glasses” theme, a heart-filled intro animation, and added closing pages (long-distance→family story + final Valentine greeting with last note box).
architectural_notes: Implement the experience as a slideshow-style multi-section single-page app or routed multi-page flow with consistent animated transitions.
Provide user-editable placeholders for photos and the final custom message content.
Ensure mobile-first responsive design and touch-friendly button sizes.
Background audio should include user controls and graceful handling of autoplay restrictions.
Love Letters should support 6 cards, each with an editable note field in addition to the photo placeholder and caption.
Implement Page 1 branching state to track repeated NO clicks (first triggers gag + reset; subsequent fades/disables NO).
Final page includes an additional animated story sequence (long-distance to marriage) as part of the slideshow ending.
Update the slideshow flow to 9 pages by splitting the initial welcome/message/question into separate pages and inserting a new moonrise envelope/letter reveal page after the proposal.
Add a short pre-Page-1 intro animation (lightweight, fast, and consistent with existing transition style).

Update the slideshow controller/content model to support an 11-page flow (including new Pages 10–11) and a consistent “cute boy with glasses” theme, while preserving smooth transitions and music autoplay-gating behavior.

existing_features.title: Create a mobile-friendly, single-page slideshow-style Valentine’s Day experience with 6 sequential screens (Welcome, Happy Panda, Love Letters Gallery, Kiss Panda, Proposal Panda, Final Custom Message) and smooth animated transitions between screens.

Apply a cohesive visual theme across the entire site: soft pastel palette (pink/white/lavender), cute panda/romance motifs, gentle shadows/glow, and consistent typography and spacing; avoid any blue/purple-dominant styling.

Implement global ambient animations: floating hearts and sparkles overlay in the background across all screens, with performance-safe behavior on mobile (reasonable particle count) and a reduced-motion fallback that respects the user’s OS setting.

Add gentle romantic background music that loops and includes an always-visible mute/unmute control; music should begin only after a user gesture (e.g., clicking YES/Continue) to satisfy browser autoplay policies.

Screen 1 (Welcome): Display large text “Hey cutie ❤️”, then fade in the message “You make my world brighter every day… and I want to ask you something special.”, then show the question “Will you be my Valentine?” with two buttons: “YES 💖” and “NO 😠”.
Screen 1 (NO path): When “NO 😠” is clicked, show an angry cartoon panda animation and the text “Wrong answer! Try again 😤🐼”, then automatically return to the same question state after a short delay.
Screen 1 (YES path): When “YES 💖” is clicked, play a heart confetti animation and transition to Screen 2.

Screen 2 (Happy Panda): Show a happy dancing panda animation with the text “You just made me the happiest person alive! 🐼💞” and a “Continue” button with sparkly styling/animation that moves to Screen 3.

Screen 3 (Love Letters Gallery): Display 4 large love letters side-by-side (envelope/card style). Each letter opens when clicked with a cute opening animation and floating hearts. Inside each opened letter, show a photo placeholder frame (no upload required) and the captions in this order: “My favorite smile”, “My happy place”, “My forever girl”, “My heart”. Include a “Continue ❤️” button to proceed to Screen 4.

Screen 4 (Kiss Panda): Show a cute panda blowing kisses animation. Fade in the text “If I could, I’d kiss you a thousand times right now 💋🐼” and render soft heart particles in the background. Include a Continue button to proceed to Screen 5.

Screen 5 (Proposal Panda): Show a panda kneeling with a ring animation and the big text “Will you marry me someday? 💍”. Provide exactly two positive buttons: “Of course ❤️” and “Always ❤️” (no negative option). Either selection advances to the Final screen with a romantic transition.

Final Screen (Custom Message): Provide a beautiful final page with floating hearts, a glowing text box labeled “My message to you…” where the user can type a custom message, and an ending line that reads “Forever yours.”
Add basic accessibility and usability polish: readable contrast for pastel UI, keyboard focus states for buttons/cards, and tap targets sized appropriately for mobile.

Standardize the entire Valentine slideshow experience to a consistent cute bunny theme (visual assets and user-facing copy), removing mixed panda/bunny references across all screens while keeping the existing 6-screen slideshow flow, pastel palette, ambient hearts/sparkles, transitions, and background music behavior intact.

Update Screen 1 (Welcome) NO-path behavior: on the first NO click, show an angry cartoon bunny animation and the text “Wrong answer! Try again 😤🐼”, then automatically return to the question state; on a second attempt to click NO, make the NO option fade out and become disabled/unselectable.

Expand Screen 3 (Love Letters Gallery) from 4 to 6 love letter cards, keeping the same envelope/card style and open-on-click animation with floating hearts, and use the following captions in this exact order: “My favorite smile”, “My happy peace”, “My forever girl”, “My heart”, “My life”, “My future wifey”.

Inside each opened love letter on Screen 3, include (1) a photo placeholder area where the user can paste a photo and (2) an editable notes box where the user can type a personal note for that letter.

Update Screens 2, 4, and 5 to bunny-themed visuals and requested copy updates: Screen 2 text must read “You just made me the happiest person alive! Bunny 💞”; Screen 4 text must read “If I could, I’d kiss you a thousand times right now 💋 Bunny”; Screen 5 remains “Will you marry me someday? 💍” with two affirmative buttons only, and includes a cute happy-bunny animation accent on selection before advancing.

Enhance the Final Page by adding an embedded, cartoon-style animated story sequence depicting a long-distance relationship evolving into love and marriage (a short multi-step animation), displayed alongside the existing “My message to you…” editable text box and the “Forever yours.” ending line.
Add the newly generated bunny and expanded love-letter/story images as static assets under frontend/public/assets/generated and update the frontend to reference these new filenames.

Restructure the Valentine slideshow from the current 6-screen flow into a 9-page flow: (1) “Hey cutie ❤️” + Continue, (2) fading romantic message “You make my world brighter every day… and I want to ask you something special.” + Continue, (3) Valentine question “Will you be my Valentine?” with YES/NO behavior (first NO shows angry bunny gag then returns; second NO disables/fades NO), (4) Happy bunny + Continue, (5) Love Letters (6 cards) + Continue, (6) Kiss bunny + Continue, (7) Proposal bunny with two positive buttons, (8) Moonrise envelope/letter reveal with editable content + Continue, (9) Final custom message page with the long-distance-to-family animated story.
Implement Page 1 as a dedicated intro screen that shows only the large text “Hey cutie ❤️” and a Continue button.
Implement Page 2 as a dedicated intro screen where the message “You make my world brighter every day… and I want to ask you something special.” fades in, and a Continue button advances to Page 3.

Implement Page 3 as the dedicated Valentine question screen with the exact question “Will you be my Valentine?” and two buttons “👉 YES 💖” and “👉 NO 😠”, keeping the existing NO/YES behavior: first NO shows an angry cartoon bunny animation and the text “Wrong answer! Try again 😤🐼” then returns to the question; second NO attempt fades out and becomes disabled/unselectable; YES triggers heart confetti then advances to Page 4.

Add a new Page 8 screen after Proposal acceptance: show an envelope/letter-box opening sequence with a moonrise animation, then reveal a letter/page emerging from the envelope containing an editable text area where the user can write anything, and a Continue button to advance to the final page.

Extend the final animated story sequence to depict: long-distance → love → marriage → family with 5 children, in a beautiful cartoon style, and ensure it is displayed on the final page alongside the existing “My message to you…” editable text box and “Forever yours.” ending line.

Ensure all user-facing copy and screen labels are consistent with the cute bunny theme across all pages (remove remaining mixed panda references in text where present), while keeping the user-requested exact phrases unchanged where explicitly specified.

Update the slideshow controller so it supports 9 pages, including the new Page 8 and the split intro pages, while preserving the existing transition timing behavior and the onUserInteraction callback behavior used for music autoplay gating.
Add a tiny intro animation that plays automatically before Page 1 (the "Hey cutie ❤️" screen) to make the opening feel sweeter, then seamlessly reveals Page 1 when finished.
Ensure the pre-Page 1 intro animation respects reduced-motion preferences by using an instantaneous or minimal-motion fallback when the OS setting "prefers-reduced-motion: reduce" is enabled.

Update the slideshow flow from the current 9 screens to an 11-page flow with the following order and navigation: (Pre-intro animation) → Page 1 (HEY JAAN ❤️ + Continue) → Page 2 (fading romantic message + Continue) → Page 3 (Valentine question YES/NO behavior) → Page 4 (happy dancing boy + Continue) → Page 5 (Love Letters x6 + Continue ❤️) → Page 6 (kiss boy + Continue) → Page 7 (proposal boy with two affirmative buttons) → Page 8 (moonrise envelope + editable letter + Continue ❤️) → Page 9 (custom message + Forever yours.) → Page 10 (full animated story long-distance→love→marriage→family with 5 children) → Page 11 (final Valentine greeting + last note box).
Implement the new Page 1 welcome screen copy exactly as “HEY JAAN ❤️” (uppercase as shown) with a Continue button, replacing the existing “Hey cutie ❤️” copy.

Update Page 3 (Valentine question) to the “cute boy with glasses” theme: on the first NO click, show an angry cartoon boy with glasses animation and the text exactly “Wrong answer! Try again 😤”, then automatically return to the question state; on the second NO attempt, fade out and disable the NO option; on YES, transition to Page 4 with a celebratory heart + stars + moon confetti-style effect.

Update Page 4 to show a happy dancing cartoon boy with glasses (not bunny/panda) and display the text exactly “You just made me the happiest person alive!  💞” (including the double space before the emoji as provided), with a sparkly Continue button.

Update Page 6 (Kiss) to the “cute boy with glasses” theme: show a boy with glasses blowing kisses animation; fade in the text exactly “If I could, I’d kiss you a thousand times right now 💋 ” (including the trailing space shown), with soft heart particles floating in the background, and a Continue button.

Update Page 7 (Proposal) to the “cute boy with glasses” theme: show a boy with glasses kneeling with a ring animation; update the proposal question text exactly to “Will you marry me in future? 💍”; provide exactly two affirmative buttons: “👉 Of course ❤️” and “👉 Always ❤️”; selecting either shows a cute happy boy-with-glasses celebration accent then advances to Page 8.

Refactor the current final page so Page 9 is a dedicated “Custom Message” page (with a cute boy-with-glasses animation on the page), containing a glowing text box labeled exactly “My message to you…”, floating hearts, and the romantic ending line exactly “Forever yours.” (without extra emoji).

Add a new Page 10 that presents a full animated story sequence in a beautiful cartoon style that depicts: long-distance → love → marriage → family with 5 children. The story must be viewable on mobile and must respect reduced-motion preferences (no auto-advance when reduced motion is enabled).
Add a new Page 11 closing screen that displays the text exactly “Happy Valentine Day my love my future wifey” and includes an editable note box where the user can write a final note.
Update the pre-Page 1 intro animation to match the requested theme “Happy Valentine Day love with hearts” while keeping the existing reduced-motion fallback behavior intact.
Remove remaining bunny/panda references from user-facing copy and alt text across all pages being updated, and standardize the experience to a consistent “cute boy with glasses” theme throughout.
